ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Budding yeast belongs to unicellular eukaryotes. To search for genes related to the regulation of protein secretion, scientists used acid phosphatase (P enzyme) as an indicator to screen yeast protein secretion mutants and studied them. Chemical mutagens were used for treatment, and a mutant strain with abnormal protein secretion (sec1) was screened from yeast. Phosphate-free culture medium can promote the secretion of yeast P enzyme, and the activity of P enzyme secreted extracellularly can reflect the amount of P enzyme. Yeast was placed in phosphate-free culture medium, and the extracellular P enzyme detection results for sec1 and the wild type are shown in the figure below. According to the figure, at 24℃, the extracellular P enzyme of sec1 and the wild type increases with time. After transfer to 37℃, what trend does the extracellular P enzyme of sec1 show?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis is time (h), and the vertical axis is P enzyme activity per milligram of protein; the black solid-point curve is labeled sec1, and the hollow-point curve is the wild type. ② indicates transfer to 37℃ culture, located at about after 2 h; ③ indicates transfer back to 24℃ and addition of a protein synthesis inhibitor, located at about 4.5 h. Observing the sec1 black-point curve after ② and before ③, the value first rises from about 17 to about 20, and then decreases to about 12 and about 10. Reasoning: The question stem states that extracellular P enzyme activity can reflect the amount of extracellular P enzyme, so after transfer to 37℃, the trend of extracellular P enzyme amount in sec1 is consistent with the black-point curve, namely first rising and then falling.
